transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... for almost two years now, I've just had this absolute certainty that ever since that big commission, a few people in my ensemble have been quietly trying to undermine my work. They do it through, you know, sudden schedule changes, or how they choose their seating, or just these little comments during rehearsals. And they'll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, but... I mean, I know what's going on. 

It's like when the violas suddenly decide to sit further back. Which, by the way, completely ruins the acoustics. I actually spent a huge chunk of grad school focusing specifically on spatial acoustics and resonance. The hall we rehearse in right now has this terrible reverb anyway, especially near the HVAC vents on the east wall. The building manager told me he’d fix those vents last October, but he never did. I think he just doesn't care about the space, honestly. I've tried telling him that the temperature fluctuations knock the woodwinds out of tune, and he just looks at me blankly. But... anyway, yeah, the ensemble members, they just keep doing these little things to sabotage the pieces I write, and I can't shake it.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people couldn't see or hear?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear imaginary voices or see things that aren't there. Though, to be fair, I do hear things other people don't, but that's just because I have perfect pitch. It's actually a bit of a curse sometimes. 

Like, just yesterday I was at the coffee shop near the conservatory, and their espresso machine has this high-pitched whine that sits exactly a quarter-tone sharp of B flat. It's excruciating. I tried to tell the barista that her pressure valve was probably wearing out—you can always tell by the frequency shift when the seal gets loose—but she just gave me this totally blank stare. It's impossible to sit in there and review a score with that constant dissonant hum in the background. It honestly amazes me how people can just tune out their sonic environment like that. Most people just walk around with earbuds in anyway, listening to heavily compressed audio files that completely destroy the dynamic range of a recording, so I guess they don't notice. 

But... wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking me? Oh, right. No, no voices or anything like that. Just the music and, well, the espresso machines.
Outside of your ensemble, do you feel that other people in your life, such as friends or family, are also working against you or untrustworthy?

No, no, it's really just the people in the ensemble. My friends and family are fine. I mean, my parents don't always get what I do, but they're supportive. They actually came out for the premiere of that big commission I mentioned. My mom insisted on taking us all out to dinner afterward at this Italian place downtown. 

Which, by the way, was a disaster acoustically. They had these hard tile floors and bare brick walls, and the ambient noise level was easily pushing 80 decibels. You literally couldn't hear the person sitting across from you without shouting. I don't understand why restaurant designers don't incorporate acoustic panels or at least some soft furnishings. It completely ruins the dining experience when all you can hear is the clatter of silverware bouncing off the ceiling. I actually drew up a little sketch on my napkin of how they could install some baffles near the ceiling to absorb the sound, but I obviously didn't give it to the manager. 

But anyway, yeah, my family is fine. They're not trying to sabotage me or anything. It's just the ensemble.
